revisions.change: Bounded backward transcript paging and append-aware native history identity.
Retriable native-source churn, structured interruption, and history-reset semantics.
Bounded inline and opaque-staged multi-attachment prompt transactions.
Pre-session model catalogs and exact optional model selection for immediate and scheduled creation.
Optional normalized tool semantics for command, file-read, search, and web-lookup families.

Optional bounded large-history replay fields: shortened-body marking on model-output/thinking/user-message, a bounded-tail-only snapshot sink declaration, skipped-record reporting on a capture, and snapshot-sink state-authority suppression after accepted messages settle.
Stable SESSION_CREATE_TEMPORARILY_UNAVAILABLE error code for bounded agent-startup readiness failures.
Stable DRIVE_OWNERSHIP_UNKNOWN and DRIVE_NATIVE_SESSION_UNRESUMABLE codes for distinct reason-tagged Drive refusal feedback.
Session-level owner projection, socket-local mutation authority, revision-conditional cross-client Drive joins, and acknowledged terminal handoff.
IntegrationKind gains http-websocket for Kimi Code, plus an unknown fallback member so a client degrades one unrecognized roster row instead of failing the whole roster decode.

SessionDriveControl gains handoffAvailable, takeoverAvailable and takeoverMode so control availability is declared as data instead of inferred, plus an unknown AttachMode fallback so an unrecognized mode degrades to read-only rather than aborting a session decode.
Authenticated clients exchange header credentials for single-use WebSocket authorization tickets through /api/ws-auth-tickets; long-lived query credentials are no longer accepted.
revisions.compatibilityChange: The broker requires revision 16 clients because revision 15 cannot acquire WebSocket authorization tickets. The revision 16 client supports the revision 15 query-credential broker only for the client-first rollout, and refuses older brokers before placing a long-lived credential in a URL.

revisions.change: Authenticated artifact downloads are principal-bound, and clients can refresh a short-lived artifact ticket through /api/sessions/{tool}/{session}/artifact/{artifact}/ticket.
revisions.compatibilityChange: The broker requires revision 17 clients because revision 16 clients do not attach their active credential to artifact downloads. The revision 17 client remains compatible with revision 16 brokers during the client-first rollout.

revisions.change: Owners can inspect and change the authenticated HTTP workspace-browsing exposure gate through /api/broker/features/workspace-browsing; enabling requires explicit remote-file-access confirmation and a broker restart. Model catalogs may advertise a human-facing provider/profile label while retaining the exact native provider identity. Permission requests may advertise a distinct persistent-rule approval decision.

First-party clients add complete omp roster identity, agent color, and New Session support. Brokers use revision 19 as omp's visibility floor so revision-18 clients do not receive a second-class omp row.

Clients can read an aggregated, read-only usage report for one date window through /api/tokdash/report. The broker projects Tokdash's usage, active-time and composite insights scans into one DTO by explicit field selection, so prompt text (display_name) cannot cross the wire, and serves the period token total beside the project facet rows so a client can reconcile the share of tokens the facet does not cover. Project names are owner-only: an observe-scoped principal is served the same report with the project facet withheld. The requested window is bounded in span and its upstream scans are capped in concurrency. Adding the route moves the registry surface hash; the route is additive and raises no minimum. Note that 18 is the revision shipped clients advertise, so a revision-19-or-later client ships before this broker.

The usage report carries the Tokdash that produced it: its running version, the minimum version the report is built against, and whether the running build is below it. A Tokdash older than that floor publishes no window verdict at all, which is not the same fact as a current one refusing the requested period, and without this block a client cannot tell the two apart and blames the period. No route, frame kind, message type or error code changes, so the surface hash holds and no minimum moves; a revision-20 client that never reads the block behaves exactly as before.

Creation requests may carry an exact adapter-advertised permission mode, agents expose a pre-session mode catalog route, roster rows distinguish display rename from native rename, adapter-authored SessionInfo snapshots are decoded strictly before publication, and OMP native-version attestation failures carry a stable typed error code.

The /api/sessions roster carries `complete`. The broker now bounds how long a caller waits for a slow discovery leg and answers with the legs that have landed, so for the first time a roster can be served that is not the whole roster; a client that reads every roster as an authoritative replacement would render the shortfall as sessions that do not exist. `complete` is false for a sweep still running and for a settled sweep that did not read every adapter -- a leg abandoned at its budget, or one that threw. Row count does not enter into it: such a leg returns the carry of the last sweep that DID read the adapter, which cannot mention anything that appeared since. Measured on a real installation as an agent absent from its own roster while registered and creatable. The field adds no route, frame kind, message type or error code, so the surface hash is unchanged from revision 22; the number moves because the DTO did. The minimum client revision stays at 17, and the broker enforces what that claim requires: the EARLY answer -- short because the sweep is still running -- is served only to a caller declaring revision 23 or later, so an older client waits for the sweep exactly as it did against a revision-22 broker. A settled sweep that lost a leg is still served to everyone, because that condition predates this revision and persists while the adapter is down; removal deltas are withheld for the lost adapter for every client alike, since deltas carry no completeness of their own.

question-request carries an optional `blocking` flag so an adapter can surface an asynchronous question (Codex delivery:"async" agent items) that stays visible and answerable without forcing the session into needs-input; omission reproduces the pre-24 blocking behavior. The answer transport stays adapter-owned: a native RPC request is answered with its RPC response, an async question is steered in as user input. The flag adds no route, frame kind, message type or error code, so the surface hash is unchanged from revision 22; the number moves because the DTO did. The minimum client revision stays at 17: an older client ignores the field and renders the same card, and only the broker reads the flag.

`agent-activity` gains the `command` kind, a bounded `output` tail and an `exitCode`, so a shell command the agent launched in the background is visible while it runs and reports how it ended. Such a command outlives the turn that started it, which is why it needs a surface at all: the transcript records the launch with an empty result body and never updates it, so today a job that runs for forty minutes is indistinguishable from one that never started. The kind also carries a different lifetime, now stated in the message's doc comment -- a subagent or workflow retires its live surface on a terminal frame, while a command's terminal frame persists until the reader dismisses it, because how it ended is the fact the card exists to deliver. `exitCode` is present only when the tool reported one and is never synthesized from a status. No route, frame kind, message type or error code changes, so the surface hash is unchanged from revision 22; the number moves because the DTO did. The minimum client revision stays at 17: an older client decodes an unrecognized kind as its generic activity value and ignores fields it does not read, so it renders the card with a title and a status exactly as it renders any other activity.
